items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the relation v_f = v_i + at.

rubric.why: The graph represents the initial and final velocities over the time interval.
rubric.description: Identify the initial and final velocities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying v_i at t = 0 and v_f at time t.

rubric.why: Acceleration is the slope of a velocity-time graph.
rubric.description: Relate acceleration to the graph’s slope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a = (v_f − v_i)/t.

rubric.why: Multiplying the acceleration relation by t gives the change in velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining at = v_f − v_i.
Award 1 mark for correctly obtaining v_f = v_i + at.

modelAnswer: On a velocity-time graph, let the initial velocity be v_i at t = 0 and the final velocity be v_f at time t.
Acceleration is the slope of the graph: a = (v_f − v_i)/t.

items.followUp: A force of 30 N acts on a square surface of side 5 mm. Calculate the pressure on the surface.

rubric.why: The applied force is given in the question.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying F = 20 N.

rubric.why: The side length must be expressed in SI units before calculating the area.
rubric.description: Convert the side length to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting 10 mm to 0.01 m.

rubric.why: The area of a square is the side length squared.
rubric.description: Calculate the square area in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining A = 1 × 10^-4 m^2.

rubric.why: Pressure is force divided by area, using the given force and calculated area.
rubric.description: Write the formula and substitute the values with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using P = F/A and substituting 20 N and 1 × 10^-4 m^2.

rubric.why: Dividing 20 N by 1 × 10^-4 m^2 gives the pressure.
rubric.description: Give the pressure with its correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N; side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.
Area of the square, A = side^2 = (0.01 m)^2 = 1 × 10^-4 m^2.

items.followUp: Give two examples of difficulties people would face if friction disappeared.

rubric.why: Friction between the feet and the ground provides the grip needed for walking.
rubric.description: State what would happen to walking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that walking would become impossible or that feet would slip without friction.

rubric.why: Friction is needed for braking and for practical actions such as holding objects and writing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid consequence, such as vehicles being unable to stop with brakes, difficulty holding objects, or inability to write.

modelAnswer: Walking would become impossible because there would be no friction between our feet and the ground to provide grip.
Vehicles could not be stopped by their brakes because friction between the brakes and wheels would be absent.
